newsitem.title: CANADA: No rush in N.America to copy Delta surcharge cut.
newsitem.headline: No rush in N.America to copy Delta surcharge cut.

text.p: Major North American airlines say they are not planning at this point to match Delta Airlines decision to drop its fuel surcharge on cargo shipments.
Officials of American Airlines, United Airlines, Northwest Airlines and Air Canada said they were watching Delta's move but had no plans to drop or amend their own surcharges.
"We have no plans at this time to drop our surcharge," said Northwest spokesman Doug Killian. "Our fuel costs are still high and we're still not covering those additional costs without the surcharge.
"Fuel prices in our estimation have not really stabilized yet."

AA Cargo vice-president Mark Najarian echoed that view: "Our fuel costs, have they come down a little bit? Yes, a little bit, but (are) nowhere near where they were before the prices started going up again".
Further moderation was expected over the course of 1997, and maybe by fall would be where they were before last year's big run-up, he said.
At the same time, all carriers say North Atlantic traffic is exceptionally strong, and that has Delta's competitors scratching their heads about the airline's motive for dropping the surcharge.
"If we're doing well, they (Delta) have to be in the same position," said one US carrier official. "I can't believe they're hurting.
"I talked to some customers about what reason Delta was giving them (for dropping the surcharge) and none of them really gave me a good answer."
